I think I may have approved too quickly a PR by <@363800010518822915>! <@363800010518822915> when validating the bid, at an epoch boundary the builder may not have funds to cover the bid after the epoch transition. And it's balance will be different with and without the parent block applied, so perhaps the thing of allowing the bid to propagate may actually cause some disconnections because of the balance thing 🙁 > cause some disconnections because of the balance thing huh? isn't that ignore? but yes you need to run epoch transition due to pending payments hmm but why is it `IGNORE` that's strange, seems like a reject rule to me yeah I assumed it was when replying here 🙂 let's make it a reject then, seems wrong not to cc <@592004585506340885> perhaps whomever wrote that was smart enough to know validators would use different states to validate the bid ignoring is safer > would use different states to validate the bid not different, wrong states yeah, agreed, still ignoring is safer state regen to validate a p2p bid is just stupid well, we need to catch false rejects before mainnet it's going to be tricky to trigger (even realize this edge case exists) on a real scenario. Happy to realize we may have this bug live right now because you pinged me on your PR gossip validation specs tests can catch this more easily <@586161934425128960> so do we want to keep this as ignore or change it to reject? It's unclear to me if potuz's comment changed your thoughts here. Add it to the agenda today Justin Added. Let us know. You were the author of this line 😄 this should be a reject imo, client should use the right state to validate stuff 🤷 Pretty sure I agree. But let's chat more at acdt. otherwise I am not sure hwo to reason about ignore vs. reject if we assume sloppy client code with gossip validation spec tests covering this we should be in a much better spot do we wanna discuss this too https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9756 ? <@412614104222531604> will deathstar be revived for devnet-7? the ehtrex instance seems cooked to me, not sure how to recover it, otherwise we can keep testing epoch boundary reorgs on the next devnet I thought so 😄 It will lead to a lot of ignores anyway, I'm sure as hell that won't evaluate any bid with any state that is not by current head state, unadvanced rejects have bitten us numerous times already we definitely don't want to have 2 epoch transitions due to bids, so lodestar will drop those too with my pr but we have gossip validation spec tests now > that won't evaluate any bid with any state that is not by current head state, unadvanced I do wonder about this, becasue we saw the node being "dossed" by bids at the boundary that was a reason why we missed slot 0 bids from the report that <@577788234810130432> did 🙏 I think what you guys want becomes effectively impossible. Suppose I get a bid for parent instead of head, and the head was built by the sabe builder. Then the balance would not cover it for the head state, but it will for the parent since without applying the head state the balance will be different. So to actually verify the bid correctly I would have to load the parent state instead of the head state. Which means I **will never ever** let a bid for the parent block, which is something you guys wanted to start with. > would have to load the parent state instead of the head state yes, what's the problem with this, we have it cached, it's really cheap we don' t and I'm certain I'll push to ignore these if clients decide to ignore message if it's too expensive to validate a message that is fine though? we may have it cached in the hot state cache, but again relying on even loading this state worries me we should not have to pick anything but head for this. I think it's much simpler to just be lax on this becasue you don't have tree states? because it requires the extra complexity of checking if the state is in the hot state cache, it will pick probably unpaged memory, removing something that I may need on the head state from the L2 cache, etc... complicating my life and my normal block processing for bid validation is crazy And spectests aren't a silver bullet here. To test this very simple edge case you'll need to cook up the situation in which the builder gets a block and then bids in the next one to reorg it's own block and bids more than what it would have had left if the head block is included. This is just one edge case, do you think you'll get all of them accounted for in unit tests? > do you think you'll get all of them accounted for in unit tests? <@592004585506340885> 😄 Yes, eventually. Though ordering might be an issue. for us this should be `O(1)` but I let <@575994543527297055> chime in, and also other clients, I don't see an issue with allowing bids for parent prysm never computes a state to validate a bid, it looks up next slot cache and if the state is not there we just ignore `NextSlotStateReadOnly(bid.parent_root, bid.slot)` I think that's the right thing to do the problem is that the NSC will have the state but not advanced in the usual case so we will just always ignore these But Is that really bad though? I much prefer not getting dos'ed then forward p2p bids with few chance of winning sure but the point is that we can just use the head state I think <@755590043632140352> what do you mean you do this on mainnet? https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/commit/3cf9687dd9b5018ab3eeb7c474794aea38a63335 yeah that PR is for our production code

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I think what you guys want becomes effectively impossible. Suppose I get a bid for parent instead of head, and the head was built by the sabe builder. Then the balance would not cover it for the head state, but it will for the parent since without applying the head state the balance will be different. So to actually verify the bid correctly I would have to load the parent state instead of the head state. Which means I **will never ever** let a bid for the parent block, which is something you guys wanted to start with.

This is just one edge case, do you think you'll get all of them accounted for in unit tests?
